objects.text: The service shall use only the Python standard library.

The service shall follow this interface. `python -m homelab_home` serves HTTP on `$HOMELAB_HOME_BIND:$HOMELAB_HOME_PORT` (bind `127.0.0.1` by default). The configuration is a TOML file named by `HOMELAB_HOME_CONFIG`: one `[[service]]` table per service with the strings `name`, `url`, `category`. In a `url`, `{host}` stands for the host name of the request (its `Host` header without the port); for a check it stands for `$HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST` (`127.0.0.1` by default). `GET /` answers an HTML page: every service grouped by category (categories in the order of their first appearance in the file), each as a link to its URL, with its state. `GET /api/status` answers a JSON list, in the order of the file, of objects with `name`, `category`, `url` (with `{host}` replaced), `state`, `response_ms`, `checked_at`. `state` is `up`, `slow` or `down`: up when the service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within `HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS` milliseconds (default 3000), slow when it answers so but after `HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS` milliseconds (default 1000), down otherwise (no answer in time, a refused connection, a status of 500 or more). `response_ms` is an integer, `null` when down; `checked_at` is ISO 8601 local time. The service checks every service at start, then every `HOMELAB_HOME_INTERVAL` seconds (default 30). `GET /api/history` answers a JSON list, in the order of the file, of objects with `name`, `checks` (the number of checks kept from the last `HOMELAB_HOME_WINDOW_SECONDS` seconds, 3600 by default; older checks are dropped) and `availability` (the percentage of them that found the service up or slow, rounded to one decimal).
The system shall list, on `GET /`, every service of the configuration file named by `HOMELAB_HOME_CONFIG`, grouped by category, each as a link to its URL.
The system shall check every configured service and report, on `GET /api/status`, as JSON, its state (`up`, `slow` or `down`, as CTR-02 defines them) and its response time in milliseconds.
The system shall report as `slow` a service that answers after the threshold named by `HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS`.
The system shall keep the checks of the last hour and report, on `GET /api/history`, the availability of each service over that hour, as a percentage.
The system shall replace `{host}` in a configured URL by the host name the page was opened with.
The system shall listen on the address named by `HOMELAB_HOME_BIND`, `127.0.0.1` by default.
The system shall check a URL holding `{host}` against the host named by `HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST`, `127.0.0.1` by default.

objects.title: The dashboard lists every configured service, by category
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want one page listing every service of my configuration, grouped by category and linked, so that I can reach them all from one place.

When `GET /` is requested, the system shall list every service of the configuration file named by HOMELAB_HOME_CONFIG, grouped by its category in the order the category first appears in that file, each service as a link to its URL.

objects.title: Every service is checked, with its state and response time
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want each service checked and its state and response time reported, so that I can see at a glance what is up and what is not.

When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `up` with its response time in milliseconds, on `GET /api/status`.
When a configured service answers with an HTTP status of 500 or more, or refuses the connection, the system shall report its state as `down` with a response time of `null`, on `GET /api/status`.

When a configured service accepts the connection but answers nothing within HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `down` with a response time of `null`, on `GET /api/status`.

objects.title: A late answer is reported as slow
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want a service that answers late but does answer to be reported as slow, so that I can tell a sluggish service from a broken one.

When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 but takes longer than HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `slow` with its response time in milliseconds on `GET /api/status`.
When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within the number of milliseconds named by HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS, the system shall report its state as `up`.

objects.title: Availability over the last hour
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want the availability of each service over the last hour, so that I can see whether a service has been flaky.

When `GET /api/history` is requested, the system shall answer, for every service of the configuration file and in the order of that file, the number of its checks kept from the last hour and its availability over that hour as a percentage rounded to one decimal.

When some of the kept checks found a service up or slow and others did not, the system shall report its availability as the percentage of the kept checks that found it up or slow, rounded to one decimal.
When a check is older than the number of seconds named by HOMELAB_HOME_WINDOW_SECONDS, the system shall drop it, so that `GET /api/history` reports only the checks of that window.

objects.title: Links follow the host name the page was opened with
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want the dashboard to use the host name I opened it with, so that I can reach my services from my laptop as well as from my phone.
When a configured URL contains `{host}` and `GET /` is requested with a host name, the system shall show that URL with `{host}` replaced by the host name of the request.
When a configured URL contains `{host}`, `GET /api/status` shall answer it with `{host}` replaced by the host name of the request, and the check of that service shall use `127.0.0.1`.

objects.title: The service listens where the client asks it to
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want to name the address the dashboard listens on, so that it can serve the whole local network and not only the machine itself.
When the service is started with HOMELAB_HOME_BIND naming an address, the system shall listen on that address, answering there on HOMELAB_HOME_PORT.
When HOMELAB_HOME_BIND names an address other than 127.0.0.1, the system shall not listen on 127.0.0.1, where the port refuses the connection.

objects.title: The checks go to the address the services hold
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want to name the address a {host} URL is checked against, so that a service published on the machine is seen up from a container.
When a configured URL holds {host} and HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST names an address, the system shall check that service against the address it names.

In a `url`, `{host}` stands for the host name of the request (its `Host` header without the port); for a check it stands for `$HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST` (`127.0.0.1` by default). `GET /` answers an HTML page: every service grouped by category (categories in the order of their first appearance in the file), each as a link to its URL, with its state. `GET /api/status` answers a JSON list, in the order of the file, of objects with `name`, `category`, `url` (with `{host}` replaced), `state`, `response_ms`, `checked_at`. `state` is `up`, `slow` or `down`: up when the service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within `HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS` milliseconds (default 3000), slow when it answers so but after `HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS` milliseconds (default 1000), down otherwise (no answer in time, a refused connection, a status of 500 or more). `response_ms` is an integer, `null` when down; `checked_at` is ISO 8601 local time. The service checks every service at start, then every `HOMELAB_HOME_INTERVAL` seconds (default 30). `GET /api/history` answers a JSON list, in the order of the file, of objects with `name`, `checks` (the number of checks kept from the last `HOMELAB_HOME_WINDOW_SECONDS` seconds, 3600 by default; older checks are dropped) and `availability` (the percentage of them that found the service up or slow, rounded to one decimal).
The system shall list, on `GET /`, every service of the configuration file named by `HOMELAB_HOME_CONFIG`, grouped by category, each as a link to its URL.
The system shall check every configured service and report, on `GET /api/status`, as JSON, its state (`up`, `slow` or `down`, as CTR-02 defines them) and its response time in milliseconds.
The system shall report as `slow` a service that answers after the threshold named by `HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS`.
The system shall keep the checks of the last hour and report, on `GET /api/history`, the availability of each service over that hour, as a percentage.
The system shall replace `{host}` in a configured URL by the host name the page was opened with.
The system shall listen on the address named by `HOMELAB_HOME_BIND`, `127.0.0.1` by default.
The system shall check a URL holding `{host}` against the host named by `HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST`, `127.0.0.1` by default.

objects.title: The dashboard lists every configured service, by category
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want one page listing every service of my configuration, grouped by category and linked, so that I can reach them all from one place.

When `GET /` is requested, the system shall list every service of the configuration file named by HOMELAB_HOME_CONFIG, grouped by its category in the order the category first appears in that file, each service as a link to its URL.

objects.title: Every service is checked, with its state and response time
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want each service checked and its state and response time reported, so that I can see at a glance what is up and what is not.

When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `up` with its response time in milliseconds, on `GET /api/status`.
When a configured service answers with an HTTP status of 500 or more, or refuses the connection, the system shall report its state as `down` with a response time of `null`, on `GET /api/status`.

When a configured service accepts the connection but answers nothing within HOMELAB_HOME_TIMEOUT_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `down` with a response time of `null`, on `GET /api/status`.

objects.title: A late answer is reported as slow
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want a service that answers late but does answer to be reported as slow, so that I can tell a sluggish service from a broken one.

When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 but takes longer than HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS milliseconds, the system shall report its state as `slow` with its response time in milliseconds on `GET /api/status`.
When a configured service answers with an HTTP status below 500 within the number of milliseconds named by HOMELAB_HOME_SLOW_MS, the system shall report its state as `up`.

objects.title: Availability over the last hour
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want the availability of each service over the last hour, so that I can see whether a service has been flaky.

When `GET /api/history` is requested, the system shall answer, for every service of the configuration file and in the order of that file, the number of its checks kept from the last hour and its availability over that hour as a percentage rounded to one decimal.

When some of the kept checks found a service up or slow and others did not, the system shall report its availability as the percentage of the kept checks that found it up or slow, rounded to one decimal.
When a check is older than the number of seconds named by HOMELAB_HOME_WINDOW_SECONDS, the system shall drop it, so that `GET /api/history` reports only the checks of that window.

objects.title: Links follow the host name the page was opened with
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want the dashboard to use the host name I opened it with, so that I can reach my services from my laptop as well as from my phone.
When a configured URL contains `{host}` and `GET /` is requested with a host name, the system shall show that URL with `{host}` replaced by the host name of the request.
When a configured URL contains `{host}`, `GET /api/status` shall answer it with `{host}` replaced by the host name of the request, and the check of that service shall use `127.0.0.1`.

objects.title: The service listens where the client asks it to
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want to name the address the dashboard listens on, so that it can serve the whole local network and not only the machine itself.
When the service is started with HOMELAB_HOME_BIND naming an address, the system shall listen on that address, answering there on HOMELAB_HOME_PORT.
When HOMELAB_HOME_BIND names an address other than 127.0.0.1, the system shall not listen on 127.0.0.1, where the port refuses the connection.

objects.title: The checks go to the address the services hold
objects.text: As the owner of a homelab, I want to name the address a {host} URL is checked against, so that a service published on the machine is seen up from a container.
When a configured URL holds {host} and HOMELAB_HOME_CHECK_HOST names an address, the system shall check that service against the address it names.
